coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 11 units (domain root + 14.01..14.10), 64 .md files — matches the expected 11/64 exactly. Every file was read. The domain totals 1.21 MB; the nine largest feature files (45–69 KB each) were read with long narrative table cells (Deep Think Annotations rationale and Cross-Cut Notes prose, typically 600–2000 chars per cell) elided in the middle, keeping the opening claim and the closing consequence of each cell verbatim; all Behavior, Happy Path, Edge Cases, States, Decisions and Open Questions rows were read at full width. Where an elided cell looked load-bearing for a candidate finding it was re-read in full (14.03.01 D-12, 14.04.01 D-05/D-06/D-10, 14.02.01 D-07/D-10, 14.09.03 Behavior). moscow-ledger.md and ideation/meta were consulted only to verify cross-references made by files inside this domain. Dimensions 1 (Problem Clarity), 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are N/A for every unit in this domain — they are owned by ideation/meta/{problem-statement,personas,constraints,competitive-landscape}.md, which this domain references rather than defines. Dimensions 3, 5, 7 and 8 apply to all 11 units, giving 44 applicable checkpoints. Raw score 8.0 points / 44 = 18.2%. This tree is unusually well remediated: the dominant residual failure mode is not missing specification but decisions that were ratified in one feature file and never propagated into the sibling file that owns the mechanism (findings 001–005, 008).

findings.claim: Re-purchase after revocation is simultaneously mandated and forbidden. 14.02.01 D-07 states 'One entitlement per product per holder, always', the record is indelible (D-08), and the lifecycle table allows `revoked` -> `active` only via a successful appeal. 14.01.01's buyer-state table and edge cases require a live buy control for a holder whose entitlement was revoked. Both cannot hold: honouring D-07 means the Buy control cannot mint anything; honouring 14.01.01 means a second entitlement exists for one (product, holder). Neither statement carries a marker, and 14.02.01's own edge case 'Buyer already owns the product | Blocked before payment by D-07' never defines whether a revoked record counts as 'owns'.

Row persists (D-08) | Terminal — a new purchase mints a new record |' (the carve-out exists for payment-failed and for no other terminal state)  ||  14.01-catalog-compatibility/14.01.01-digital-product-listing-spec-sheet.md:75 — '| Owns it and it was revoked (14.09.03) | `Buy — £X`, no history shown; revocation is not a purchase bar |'  ||  same file:134 — '| Buyer's purchase was refunded and the licence revoked (14.09.03) | Listing renders normally with a live buy control. Revocation removed an entitlement; it is not a purchase bar | Buyer: standard listing. No "you refunded this" shaming. |'
findings.forcedInvention: Whether 'one entitlement per product per holder' is scoped to active entitlements or to all records; and, if a re-purchase is permitted, whether it mints a second record (violating D-07's stated rationale of one seat pool and one terms lineage) or reactivates the revoked one outside the appeal path (violating the state machine).
findings.unit_note: Both 14.02.01 and 14.01.01 are MUST-band; the collision is inside the launch set.

findings.claim: 14.09.03 owns revocation and enumerates a closed set of three triggers that excludes `chargeback`, while 14.02.01 D-10 requires chargeback to be recorded as a distinct trigger 'everywhere ... and 14.09.03's revocation'. 14.02.01's own cross-cut note names the gap as unfixed, and it was never landed. 14.02.04's chargeback edge case additionally cites a state value `revoked/reversed` that neither 14.09.03's States table nor 14.02.01's lifecycle table defines. findings.claim: 14.03.01 D-11 makes delivery branch on the *reason* a version was withdrawn — malicious withdrawals kill the in-flight transfer, superseded/defective ones let it complete — and its cross-cut note states that 14.08.04 must supply that reason. 14.08.04 owns rollback and models no reason field anywhere in its Behavior, States, Decisions or edge cases; its rollback edge case asserts the unqualified opposite rule. The sub-domain CX repeats the unqualified rule. The malware branch of D-11 is therefore unimplementable from the feature that owns the trigger.

findings.claim: 14.04.01 D-10 makes the contributor gate a two-question gate — the split *and* the use — and makes a refusal of the use block publish. 14.10.03 owns the contributor gate and models one question only (named contributors, percentages, agreement state); its D-02 states publish is never blocked on the contributor gate and only payout is. There is no field in 14.10.03 in which a contributor can refuse the use, so 14.04.01 D-10 cannot be executed, and the two decisions give opposite answers on whether a publish gate exists.

findings.claim: The 14.03 sub-domain CX carries three rules that its own feature files have since overridden, with no marker on the CX side, and the overrides were explicitly flagged as needing to be carried back and never were. The most consequential is the URL lifetime: CX-01 and 14.03.03 both specify a 'short-lived' download URL, while 14.03.01 D-04 specifies a stable 72-hour grant URL and states that 'short-lived URL' and 'resumable' are incompatible as phrased — the exact defect that silently turns a resume into a restart.
findings.evidence: 14.03-delivery-versioning-library/14.03-delivery-versioning-library-cx.md:24-26 (CX-01) — 'Each download is authorised against a live entitlement check ... and served via a short-lived, buyer-scoped URL.'  ||  14.03-delivery-versioning-library/14.03.01-download-delivery-resumable-transfer.md:191 — '| D-04 | **The delivery unit is a transfer grant: a stable, buyer-scoped, artifact-bound URL valid 72 h, re-authorised on every range request** | ... "short-lived URL" and "resumable" are incompatible as stated — the resume silently becomes a restart. ... **Refines CX-01's "short-lived URL" phrasing; Step 6 should carry the refinement.**'  ||  14.03-delivery-versioning-library/14.03.03-licence-portal-purchased-library.md:115 — 'Every download authorises through here, per request, against a live entitlement check, via a short-lived buyer-scoped URL (14.03.01 D-01).'  ||  14.03-cx.md:61 (CX-02 q5) — 'A vendor rolling back a version while a buyer is downloading it. The download should complete — the artifact is valid, the *recommendation* changed.' (overridden by 14.03.01 D-11 for malicious withdrawals)  ||  14.03-cx.md:100 (CX-04 q2) — 'If stamping fails: serve unmarked, or fail the download? An unmarked file silently defeats the mechanism.' (settled by 14.03.05 D-03, still posed as open)
findings.forcedInvention: The signed-URL TTL — a 5-minute URL satisfies 'short-lived' and destroys resumability for the 40–100 GB transfers that are this feature's normal case.

findings.claim: The composition rule 'most-restrictive-wins per axis' is determinate for every binary clause and undefined for the two non-binary ones. `sync_permitted` has three values where one (`separate-negotiation`) is a routing outcome rather than a point on a permissiveness scale, and `royalty_basis` carries a sub-basis (per-unit / percentage / per-stream) with no stated ordering. The composite outcome is user-visible — it decides whether a release gate returns `clear`, `clear-with-obligations` or `conflicted` — so two implementers produce different release-gate verdicts for the same record.
findings.evidence: 14.02-licensing-activation-entitlement/14.02.05-licence-terms-registry.md:47 — '**Permissions** — what the holder *may* do. Compose by **intersection** (most restrictive wins).'  ||  same file:57 — '| `sync_permitted` | yes / no / separate-negotiation → routes to domain 11 | yes |'  ||  same file:52 — '| `royalty_basis` | royalty-free / royalty-bearing (+ basis: per-unit, percentage, per-stream) | royalty-free |'  ||  same file:195 — '| D-06 | The registry owns the **composition semantics** (permissions intersect, obligations union, bounds intersect, most-restrictive-wins per axis); domains 09 and 12 own the **application** |'  ||  same file:89-90 — 'At release, the composite is computed across every placement, and the result is one of: `clear` / `clear-with-obligations` / `conflicted` / `unknown`.'
findings.forcedInvention: The restrictiveness ordering of `sync_permitted` (is `separate-negotiation` stricter or looser than `no`?) and the composite of two royalty-bearing clauses with different bases.

findings.claim: 14.01.01 makes the transfer policy a section required to publish for four of five product types, and 14.01.01 is a MUST-band feature. The feature that owns transfer policy, 14.06.01, is banded COULD — below the launch set — and the domain index restates that banding. At launch the publish gate therefore depends on a section whose owning feature does not exist, and nothing states whether the gate degrades, defaults, or blocks. The other cross-band publish dependencies in the same table (compatibility matrix, host dependencies) resolve because their consumers are banded at or below the producing feature; this one inverts.
